query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: SPS processing of a MgAlTiVFeCo high-entropy alloy at 1000°C induces surface enrichment of Al and Fe that in situ forms a dense, continuous spinel-type oxide film, thereby markedly enhancing resistance to tribo-corrosion degradation under elevated temperature and frictional conditions compared to the same alloy sintered at lower temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Nanocrystalline BCC solid-solution precursor powders of MgAlTiVFeCo produced by mechanical alloying.
generation.intervention: Spark plasma sintering at 1000°C instead of lower sintering temperatures (850–950°C).
generation.conditions: Elevated temperature environments with corrosive media (e.g., 3.5 wt% NaCl) combined with mechanical (tribological) loading.
generation.structural_mediator: In situ formation of a dense, continuous spinel-type oxide passive film via surface enrichment of Al and Fe.
generation.mechanism: High-temperature sintering promotes enrichment of specific elements at the surface, which form a robust oxide barrier that limits ion diffusion and reduces the active corrosion area, thereby shifting the corrosion mechanism from direct attack to a diffusion-controlled process, even under friction-induced wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: The 1000°C-sintered alloy will show significantly lower corrosion current density and enhanced tribo-corrosion resistance relative to samples sintered at lower temperatures, reflecting improved degradation resistance.
generation.baseline: MgAlTiVFeCo alloys sintered at 850–950°C that exhibit a single capacitive arc in EIS, indicating a direct-attack corrosion mechanism with higher corrosion activity.
generation.boundary: The enhanced resistance is expected under conditions replicating the SPS processing parameters; deviations in sintering temperature or alterations in alloy composition may affect passive film formation and performance.
generation.uncertainty: While improved corrosion resistance is supported by electrochemical data under static conditions, the exact magnitude of enhancement under simultaneous mechanical (tribological) loading remains to be experimentally validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate sets of MgAlTiVFeCo alloy samples using SPS at 850°C, 900°C, 950°C, and 1000°C. Subject each set to combined tribo-corrosion testing at elevated temperatures in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution while imposing a controlled sliding wear load. Compare the corrosion current densities, passive film integrity, and wear rates among the different sintering treatments.
measurements: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to quantify charge transfer and passive film resistance
Potentiodynamic polarization curves for corrosion current density
Tribological wear tests to measure wear depth and coefficient of friction
Surface characterization (XRD, SEM, EDS) to verify the presence and continuity of the spinel-type oxide film
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 1000°C-sintered samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (e.g., markedly lower corrosion current density, improved passive film integrity, and reduced tribological wear) compared to samples sintered at lower temperatures, then the hypothesis is falsified.

System: MgAlTiVFeCo lightweight high-entropy alloy (designated LW850, LW900, LW950, LW1000 based on sintering temperature). Processing: Mechanical alloying (MA) to synthesize nanocrystalline BCC solid-solution precursor powders, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 850, 900, 950, and 1000 °C.
